summary: A 40-foot tower from 1951 was replaced in 1974 by a 30-foot timber tower on an Oregon Dept. of Forestry site; unstaffed since 2016, now a remote-camera site.

facts.design: 30-foot treated timber tower with a 14-by-14-foot flat-top cab, per the register; another source says 28 feet

access.note: The spur road off Road 290 is gated, and the lookout is 0.1 miles past the gate. The state owns and operates the site, so ask ODF before visiting.

visit.trail_note: Road 290 was overgrown in 2023; the lookout is 0.1 miles past a gate on the spur road.

events.note: First tower on the site: 40-foot tower with a 14-by-14-foot house; cost $2,143.17 per the Southwest District annual report

The 40-foot tower was replaced by a 30-foot treated timber tower with a 14-by-14-foot flat-top cab; the register dates the current structure to 1974, and another source says the tower was recycled from Burnt Peak
Summer 2016 was the last season in active service, per a visit report on the register; Fire Lookout says staffed into the 2010s
Cameras installed on the tower by summer 2017; no longer staffed
Break-in; some camera equipment stolen. The source says 'last August' in a post dated 2023, so the year is inferred as August 2022
Visited July 12, 2023; found standing as a remotely monitored camera site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, Cheryl Hill and Fire Lookout give 30 feet for the 1974 tower; the Oregon Forest Lookouts page gives 28 feet. The 30-foot figure is used.
Build years differ because one count is the first 1951 tower and another is the 1974 structure now on the site. Both are recorded as events.
Fire Lookout says staffed into the 2010s, and the register's 2016 visit report calls 2016 the last active season. These agree; the 2016 date is used.
Cheryl Hill's post says 'last August' and is dated August 2023, so the year 2022 is inferred from that wording.

sources.title: White Point - Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Current status rests on a July 2023 visit; no later visit report was found. Elevation differs (4,961 ft on the register; 5,075 ft on Fire Lookout and Cheryl Hill), not carried into the story. Access is rated restricted as a judgment from the gated spur road and state ownership; the brief's access was unknown. No fire history found in these sources. Used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads.
